workflow_steps.objective: Confirm business goals, audience, positioning, markets, SKU scope, packaging formats, required outputs, stakeholders, schedule, budget, success criteria, supplied assets and unresolved decisions.

Study the Xinjiang tomato category, intended consumers, retail and ecommerce contexts, competitors, cultural and geographic references, and applicable labeling requirements without treating the published references as style direction.
Agree strategic and design principles for provenance, product appetite, trust, shelf recognition, multilingual clarity, accessibility and coherent SKU differentiation.
Define approval gates, decision owners, feedback rounds, version control, regulatory review, proofing responsibilities and the repeatable workflow for rolling the system across SKUs.
Specify the SKU architecture, package formats and dimensions, information hierarchy, panel content, variant logic, barcode zones and technical constraints for every required format.
Obtain, create or validate supplier-approved cutting, folding, seam, bleed and safe-area geometry for each confirmed package format before final artwork is built.

Develop meaningfully distinct identity and packaging directions covering naming expression, logo behavior, typography, color, imagery, provenance storytelling and representative hero-SKU applications.
Compare the directions against the agreed principles, practical constraints and prototype potential, then obtain an explicit written client choice before further development.
Produce rough physical or scale-accurate prototypes of representative packs and test shelf recognition, hierarchy, legibility, variant distinction, handling and critical panel placement.
Apply consolidated feedback and prototype findings to the selected direction while preserving approved strategic and visual decisions.
Codify the approved logo system, typography, color, graphic devices, imagery rules, multilingual behavior, minimum sizes, misuse guidance and packaging-specific governance.
Roll the approved system across all confirmed tomato-sauce variants, sizes and formats, maintaining family consistency while making each SKU clearly distinguishable.

observations: A tall Chinese-language editorial composition has a very large black headline at the top, followed by smaller text columns and substantial white space.
A wide landscape photograph shows green terrain, water and a snow-capped mountain range beneath a bright blue sky; a smaller overlapping photograph shows clusters of red tomatoes.
Lower sections visibly include a thin route or map-like line with labeled points and a separate aerial photograph dominated by long red and pale rows.
The pixels demonstrate a published outcome combining regional, agricultural and tomato-production content, but do not establish a required visual style or approved source material.
A small cylindrical metal can is shown at an angle against a light gray background with a soft shadow beneath it.
The can has a silver pull-tab lid and a predominantly red label carrying a large white wordmark, the words “Tomato Ketchup,” and a visible “30g” quantity marking.
This is visible evidence of a rendered single-package presentation for a compact tomato-product format, not a usable dieline or production specification.
A pale gray presentation board displays multiple coordinated applications, including green lanyards, red-and-white passes, business cards, tote bags and small red rectangular items.
A repeated tomato character has large oval eyes, green leaf shapes and several facial expressions; the same Latin-letter wordmark recurs across the applications.
Red, white and green visibly dominate the published application family, while some items also contain Chinese text.
The board evidences an identity extended across packaging-like items and collateral, but its wordmark, character, palette and layouts are not treated as inputs to copy.

missing_inputs: Confirmed brand name, naming rationale, Chinese and other language forms, domain availability and trademark status.
Business objectives, positioning, audience segments, price tier, sales channels, launch markets and measurable success criteria.
Complete SKU matrix covering product types, recipes or flavor variants, net weights, package formats, materials and planned future extensions.
Supplier-approved dimensions, dielines or can-label specifications, substrates, closures, print methods, ink limits, finishes, tolerances and packing-line constraints.

Mandatory legal copy, ingredients, nutrition data, allergen statements, storage instructions, manufacturer details, origin wording, date and batch fields, recycling marks and market-specific compliance requirements.
Evidence and approval for product, nutrition, sustainability, geographic-origin and certification claims.
Final barcodes and verification requirements, including required quiet zones and target symbologies.
Required languages, approved translations, transliteration rules and responsibility for linguistic and regulatory review.
Available photography, illustration, maps, product imagery and documentation of usage rights.
Competitor set, category constraints and any existing brand equity, assets or decisions that must be retained.
Required identity applications beyond packaging, final file formats, editable-source expectations and brand-guideline depth.
Budget, schedule, prototype quantity, print vendors, production volumes, stakeholders, approval authority and permitted revision rounds.
assumptions: The assignment covers creation of a new or substantially new identity and its application to a multi-SKU tomato-sauce packaging family.
No brand name, wordmark, mascot, palette, layout, copy or imagery shown in the published references is automatically part of the new solution.
The references are used only to understand visible outcome types and possible application contexts, not as source assets or a style brief.
At least one representative hero SKU and each materially different package structure will be prototyped before full-family rollout.
Production-ready masters are expected only for formats and technical specifications confirmed by the relevant suppliers.
The client or its appointed specialists will supply and approve all factual product data, regulated copy, translations, claims and barcodes.
Merchandise, campaign materials, ecommerce content and product photography are outside scope unless separately approved.
Structural invention is not assumed; existing supplier formats will be used unless structural-packaging development is explicitly commissioned.
stop_conditions: Stop before concept exploration if the brand naming status, target audience, market positioning, launch markets, initial SKU scope or final decision owner is unresolved.
Stop before dieline-dependent design if package formats, dimensions, materials or supplier-approved structural specifications are unavailable or contradictory.
Stop before family expansion until one identity and hero-pack direction has explicit written approval and prototype findings have been resolved.
Stop final artwork if mandatory copy, translations, nutrition data, claims substantiation, barcodes or regulatory approvals are incomplete.
Stop print release if trademark or asset-usage rights remain unresolved.
Stop release of any master that fails supplier preflight, barcode verification, minimum-type requirements, bleed and seam checks, color-separation checks or an agreed physical proof.
Stop delivery if final client approval, vendor technical acceptance or the agreed archive and handoff manifest has not been recorded.
rationale: The brief combines identity creation, multi-SKU packaging-system development, prototyping and manufacturing-ready handoff, so concept_to_production is more representative than a packaging rollout alone. The sequence establishes strategy and technical constraints before creative exploration, requires an explicit human selection, validates a representative pack before expansion, and gates final production on regulatory, supplier and proofing approvals. Reference analysis is confined to visible published-outcome evidence.
